2607.15200.title: Mask-Aware Policy Gradients for Diffusion Language Models
2607.15200.paper_summary: Reinforcement learning has proven effective for improving reasoning in large language models, but extending it to Masked Diffusion Language Models (MDLMs) remains challenging due to the intractability of the log-likelihood estimation. Existing approaches approximate this log-likelihood by modeling only the token predictions, ignoring the order in which positions are unmasked during generation. We observe that MDLM generation involves two decisions at each step: what tokens to place at each masked position and which positions to remask. We formalize this as a two-stage action MDP, showing that the policy gradient naturally decomposes into a token term and a masking term. Combining optimization of both terms leads to state-of-the-art outcomes on mathematical reasoning and coding benchmarks, with scores of 87.1% on GSM8K and 53.4% on MBPP.
2607.15200.paper_summary_zh: 強化學習已被證明對於改善大型語言模型的推理效果良好，但將其擴展到遮蔽擴散語言模型（MDLMs）仍然具有挑戰性，因為對數似然估計的不可處理性。現有的方法通過僅建模標記預測來近似這個對數似然，忽略了在生成過程中位置被去遮蔽的順序。我們觀察到，MDLM生成在每一步涉及兩個決策：在每個被遮蔽的位置放置什麼標記，以及哪些位置需要重新遮蔽。我們將這一過程形式化為一個兩階段行動馬爾可夫決策過程（MDP），顯示出策略梯度自然分解為標記項和遮蔽項。結合這兩個項的優化在數學推理和編碼基準上達到了最先進的結果，在GSM8K上得分87.1%，在MBPP上得分53.4%。
